Quote verbatim (Nakakura 2020, PMID 31913226). But the 3T3-L1 assay is Santen's (PharmR 603Qn020), run after its 52-week RENGE trial had shown no DUES (Aihara 2024 review, PMID 38168596); same logic the draft used for the eyelash track. Should be retro, retrodiction true.
entries.rule: Retrodiction: a model built or run after the clinic already knew the answer is retro, never same
entries.adjudication_note: Retrodiction rule: Santen's 3T3-L1 assay (603Qn020, ~2019) ran after its 52-week RENGE trial (completed pre-2018 Japanese approval) showed no DUES; reproduced it, so retro, as on the eyelash track. Draft retrodiction flag should be true.

missing: Possible retrodiction track on ocular inflammation: non-GLP monkey study 104Fq080 (report dated 2019-07-16, FDA PharmR 2022, Table 92) found laser-flare aqueous flare rising on omidenepag 0.002% monotherapy at D4/D7 versus D1 and higher with FP-agonist combination; patients: Omlonti label 5.3 'Ocular inflammation has been reported in patients taking Omlonti' (accessdata.fda.gov label/2022/215092s000lbl.pdf) and the Japanese tafluprost-combination contraindication (PMC9058248 review points to it). Run after the human signal, so it would be retro (retrodiction: true), not same. The drafter set it aside for lack of a human source, but label 5.3 is a tier 2 source.
Phase 1 healthy-volunteer IOP lowering (Aihara et al., PMID 31674861, 2019) is an engagement datum (healthy volunteers count) that the draft omits; no status change.
No admissible model source or patient failure found for aganepag isopropyl or simenepag isopropyl (searched); the draft's statement stands.

Patient-side source for the DUES/PAPS tracks predating the 3T3-L1 and organoid models: RENGE 12-month study (Jpn J Ophthalmol 2021, PMID 34495425, doi 10.1007/s10384-021-00868-y; summarized in Aihara 2024, PMID 38168596: no DUES/eyelash/iris colour change after a year) - a tier 1 patient source the safety tracks could cite.
rule_questions: SPECTRUM 3 (NCT03691649) missed its primary endpoint, noninferiority to timolol, while omidenepag's own IOP drop matched the other trials. The monkeys made no prediction against timolol. Does a missed active-comparator noninferiority primary endpoint count as an efficacy contra, or is it outside what the model predicted? The draft says outside; the rules do not say.

When the model's PD readout is the clinical endpoint itself (IOP), the engagement and efficacy cells score the same readout on different trials. Is that double counting allowed, or should engagement be untested/no_prediction?

Dose: Kirihara 2018 published the QD-sufficiency statement after Phase 2 had already used QD, but the animal work dates to 2011. Is a regimen statement first published after the trial a prospective prediction, given the model was run before?
